findings.claim: New in the correction loop: the bounded statement pass treats any value at a line end followed by a name on the next line as a missing semicolon. Valid Java that breaks a declaration after its type, such as `Book\n    a = new Book();`, is now reported in the real page as "Error, line 9: ';' expected" with the status "1 error: the compiler would reject this code". Line terminators are white space between tokens in Java, so javac accepts it. The attempt is not counted as a try, and the layout is rare for beginners, hence low; but the editor asserts a compiler error that does not exist.

evidence.section: JLS SE 25 3.6 White Space (line terminators are white space)

findings.recommendation: Do not raise ';' expected when the value at the line end is a type name and the next line continues the same declaration (next tokens are a name followed by =, ; or ,); or report that shape as not supported instead of as a compiler error.
